page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by KVM virtualization. The instance features an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. It contains 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest processing performance consistent with entry-tier multicore AMD EPYC allocations. Single-core evaluation via Geekbench records a score of 1305.0, placing it in the average tier, while multi-core performance reaches 2939.0, ranking in the lower quartile. Stress-ng scores show 767.9 for single-core and 1535.77 for multi-core compute tests. Memory bandwidth testing registers 31.36 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 16.16 GB/sec for writes. Workload tests reflect 3.57 million operations per second in Redis SET commands and 4.07 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From an architectural and cost-efficiency standpoint, the instance balances compute cores against a low memory allocation without the overhead of bundled NVMe storage. Because storage must be provisioned externally over the network, overall I/O is tied to attached cloud block storage performance and the 2 Gbps baseline network pipe. The system is structurally fitted for horizontal application scaling, lightweight web servers, compilation jobs, microservices, and general compute tasks that do not require high memory footprints or fast local scratch disk space.
